summary:
ASTRA ANALOG: Earth Analog Intelligence for Lunar Exploration

ASTRA ANALOG is a scientific web platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It explores how Earth locations can help prepare researchers and astronauts for future lunar missions.

The project compares Haughton Crater on Devon Island, Canada, with Shackleton Crater near the Moon's south pole using elevation datasets, interactive maps and terrain measurements. It examines crater depth, diameter, wall slopes, surface roughness and elevation profiles.

The platform includes a Terrain Comparison Dashboard, Mission Suitability Explorer and Evidence Explorer. These tools help users understand where Earth-based locations can support rover testing, geological research and astronaut field rehearsals.

ASTRA ANALOG also highlights scientific differences and limitations rather than presenting unsupported similarity scores. Where lunar thermal data is unavailable, it clearly communicates that gap instead of inventing results.

Our mission is to make Earth analog research more transparent, accessible and useful for planning future lunar exploration.
details:
ASTRA ANALOG — Complete Project Details

Project Name: ASTRA ANALOG
Tagline: Earth Insights. Lunar Futures.
Category: Earth and Space Science / Planetary Exploration
Challenge: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 — Identify Earth Locations that Analog the Permanent Moon Base Locations and Mars.

1. Project Overview

ASTRA ANALOG is an interactive scientific web platform that investigates how locations on Earth can help prepare scientists, engineers and astronauts for future lunar exploration.

The project compares Haughton Crater on Devon Island, Canada, with Shackleton Crater near the Moon's south pole. It examines their terrain characteristics and available surface-temperature evidence to identify where the Earth location can serve as a useful analog—and where the comparison has important limitations.

2. Problem Statement

Preparing for lunar missions is expensive and challenging. Scientists need suitable Earth locations where they can rehearse geological research, rover operations and astronaut field activities.

However, choosing an Earth analog based only on visual similarity can be misleading. Earth and the Moon have very different environments.

ASTRA ANALOG addresses this problem by providing evidence-based comparisons using scientific datasets, measurable terrain characteristics and clearly documented limitations.

3. Selected Locations

Earth Location: Haughton Crater

  • Located on Devon Island, Nunavut, Canada.
  • Situated in the Canadian High Arctic.
  • Features an impact-crater landscape and an extreme Arctic environment.
  • Has a history of use for planetary exploration research and field testing.

Moon Location: Shackleton Crater

  • Located near the lunar south pole.
  • An important region for future lunar exploration.
  • Features steep crater walls and a permanently shadowed interior.
  • Relevant to planning future lunar surface operations.

NASA previously used Haughton Crater for lunar rover field testing in 2007, making this comparison a documented research direction rather than an arbitrary location pairing. ASTRA_ANALOG_Phase1_Research_an…

4. Main Project Features

1. Interactive Site Comparison
Displays Haughton Crater and Shackleton Crater side by side using terrain maps and location information.

2. Terrain Comparison Dashboard
Examines crater diameter, depth, slopes, elevation profiles and surface characteristics.

3. Thermal Analysis
Displays seasonal surface-temperature observations from Landsat 9 for Haughton Crater. Lunar thermal comparison is marked unavailable because the required Diviner data could not be retrieved and validated within the challenge timeframe.

4. Mission Suitability Explorer
Explores how Haughton Crater may support:

  • Rover mobility testing
  • Geological field research
  • Astronaut field operations
  • Terrain testing
  • Habitat construction preparation

5. Evidence Explorer
Helps users inspect measurements, sources, methods, data quality and scientific limitations.

6. Data & Methods
Explains the scientific datasets and processing methods used in the project.

7. Limitations and Verdict
Shows where the analogy is useful and where Earth cannot reproduce lunar conditions.

5. Scientific Data Sources

The research plan identifies these datasets:

Dataset

Purpose

ArcticDEM

Earth elevation and terrain

LOLA

Lunar elevation and terrain

Landsat 8/9

Earth surface-temperature observations

MODIS

Earth land-surface-temperature context

Diviner

Lunar thermal observations; unavailable in the current analysis

The project uses scientific data rather than relying only on visual similarities.

6. Technology and Platform

The project is presented as an interactive web application with:

  • Interactive maps and visualizations
  • Terrain comparison charts
  • Scientific measurement dashboards
  • Data provenance and evidence information
  • Mission suitability tools
  • Separate navigation sections

7. Expected Impact

ASTRA ANALOG aims to make planetary analog research easier to understand and explore. It can help researchers identify useful Earth environments for rehearsing selected lunar mission activities, understand terrain differences and recognize where further scientific data is needed.

8. Important Scientific Limitation

Haughton Crater cannot fully reproduce the Moon's one-sixth gravity, vacuum, radiation environment, lack of atmosphere or extreme lunar day-night cycle. ASTRA ANALOG therefore avoids presenting a misleading universal similarity percentage.

Core message: ASTRA ANALOG does not claim that Earth is the Moon. It demonstrates how real Earth locations can help prepare us for exploring it.
